units.source_text: 左马头便接着说：“不论男女，凡下品之人，稍有一知半解，便尽量在人前夸耀，真是可厌。

en.t: The Assistant Captain of the Left Gate Guards went on: "Whether man or woman, low-bred people who know only a little will boast of it as much as they can in front of others; it is truly disagreeable.

units.source_text: 一个女子潜心钻研三史、五经[\[22\]](#part1331.html#m22)等深奥的学问，反而没有情趣。

en.t: When a woman devotes herself to studying profound subjects such as the Three Histories and the Five Classics[\[22\]](#part1331.html#m22), it instead leaves her without charm.

units.source_text: 我并不是说做女子的不应该有关于世间公私一切事情的知识。

en.t: I do not mean that a woman should have no knowledge of all the public and private affairs of the world.

units.source_text: 我的意思是：不必特地钻研学问，只要是略有才能的人，耳闻目见，也自然会学得许多知识。

en.t: What I mean is that there is no need to make a special study of scholarship; anyone with even a little ability will naturally learn a great deal simply by hearing and seeing things.

units.source_text: 譬如有的女子，汉字写得十分流丽。

en.t: For example, some women write Chinese characters with great elegance.

units.source_text: 写给女朋友的信，其实不须如此，她却一定要写一半以上的汉字，教人看了想道：

en.t: In a letter to a female friend there is really no need for that, yet she insists on writing more than half of it in Chinese characters, making the reader think:

units.source_text: 这个人没有这个毛病才好！’

en.t: If only this person did not have this fault!"

units.source_text: 写的人自己也许不觉得，但在别人读来，发音佶屈聱牙，真有矫揉造作之感。

en.t: The writer herself may not notice it, but when others read it, the pronunciation is awkward and difficult, giving a truly affected impression.

units.source_text: 这种人在上流社会中也多得很。

en.t: There are a great many such people even in high society.
